name: Jabiru
rangeDescription: West-central mexico through south america to northeastern argentina
description: Huge, massive-billed, and unmistakable stork of tropical lowlands. Found in marshes and flooded fields, but nests high in large trees.

name: Roseate Spoonbill
rangeDescription: Southern usa to northern argentina, brazil, and west indies
description: Unique pink wading bird with long, flat, spoon-shaped bill. Adults are mostly pink overall, with scarlet wing patches, orange tail, and bare pale-green head.

name: Pink-billed Parrotfinch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of viti levu (northwestern fiji)
description: A distinctive, mostly tree-dwelling finch. Body uniformly green, rump red.

name: Azores Chaffinch
rangeDescription: Azores
description: Dapper little finch endemic to the Azores, where it inhabits a range of habitats, from forests to farmlands. Handsome, brightly colored male has a blue-grayish cowl, pale orangish face and breast, and a black-and-white wing pattern (colors muted in winter).

name: Green Racquet-tail
rangeDescription: Northern philippines (lowlands of luzon and marinduque)
description: A rare medium-sized parrot of lowland and foothill forest on Luzon. The two central tail feathers have extended shafts ending in a racket shape.

name: Spotted Bowerbird
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (central queensland to western new south wales and far northwestern victoria)
description: A brownish, mottled, strongly marked bowerbird with warm brown tones overall and a small pink crest on the nape. Loud rasping calls include hisses and squawks.

name: Unicolored Antwren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (northern rio de janeiro to far northern rio grande do sul)
description: Uncommon small, short-tailed antwren of the lower and middle levels of humid forests. Very active and often follows mixed-species flocks.

name: Dusky Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters to southern mexico
description: Dull grayish flycatcher, very similar to other flycatchers, especially Hammond's and Gray. Generally grayish with green-tinged back and pale yellow wash on belly.

name: Chilean Woodstar
rangeDescription: Arid southern peru (tacna and moquegua) to northern chile (arica)
description: Tiny, highly endangered hummingbird found very locally in the desert of northern Chile. Favors native desert scrub in lowland valleys, but widely eliminated from most areas by intensive agriculture.

name: Cajamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Andes of northern peru (cajamarca)
description: Small antpitta with a restricted range in the western Andes of northwestern Peru. Note the chestnut brown plumage and pale belly; like other antpittas, it has long legs and a short tail.

name: Santa Marta Screech-Owl
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Small owl restricted to cloud forest in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Plumage is almost identical to that of Tropical Screech-Owl, with which it was confused until differences in voice were noted.

name: Nicaraguan Seed-Finch
rangeDescription: Caribbean lowlands of nicaragua, costa rica, and western panama
description: What this bird lacks in color, it makes up for with a ridiculously oversized bill. Male is all glossy black, female warm brown.

name: Gray-and-white Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru (tumbes to la libertad)
description: Small, crested flycatcher restricted to desert scrub and dry forest in lowlands and foothills of southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru. It is best identified by its bushy, split crest that shows some white when lifted.

name: Bar-winged Oriole
rangeDescription: Oak-pine scrub of southern mexico (southeastern oaxaca) to el salvador
description: Very local, poorly known black-and-yellow oriole of Chiapas and northern Central America. Favors brushy oak woodlands and semi-deciduous scrubby areas, especially with oaks.

name: Dickcissel
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern north america; winters to southern mexico to northern south america
description: Sparrowlike bird known for gathering in enormous wintering flocks in South America. Males are striking with yellow breast, black patch on throat, and rufous shoulders.

name: Friedmann's Lark
rangeDescription: Southeastern kenya and northern tanzania; status in southwestern ethiopia and northern kenya unclear
description: A small, compact lark with dark brown upperparts that appear scaly in fresh plumage, a streaked crown that can be raised as a crest, an indistinct tawny eyebrow, a striking pale throat, and a pale belly with dark breast streaks. The bill is bicolored: pale below with a dark ridge on the upper mandible.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Tibetan Sandgrouse
rangeDescription: Desert of eastern afghanistan to tibetan plateau
description: A sandy-colored ground bird with a thin needle-point tail and a gentle, dove-like profile. Not as well-marked as other sandgrouse: soft sandy brown with a light orange face and finely barred breast.

name: Reunion Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Forest of northwestern réunion (western mascarene islands)
description: Fairly small, slim cuckooshrike in which males and females are strikingly different. Males are mostly gray with black wings and tail.

name: Adamawa Turtle-Dove
rangeDescription: Highlands of eastern nigeria, northern cameroon, and far southwestern chad
description: A dark turtle-dove with typical scaly rufous-pink edging to the wings and black patches on the sides of the neck. The face is pale silvery-gray and the belly and flanks are pinkish-mauve.

name: Little Bunting
rangeDescription: Taiga of northern eurasia; winters to india, southeastern asia, and philippines
description: Small bunting with an attractive contrasting head pattern: black crown with red-brown central stripe and pale eyering. Rufous cheeks bordered by narrow black lines framing the eyes.
